issues.description: Animal is specified in the UML/problem statement with attributes `name:String` and `age:int` and a constructor `Animal(String, int)`, but the solution implements `Animal` with only `name` and a constructor `Animal(String)`. This makes the required constructor/attribute set unclear and would block students who follow the UML from matching the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the model across statement/UML and solution: either (a) update the solution to add `age:int`, add getter/setter, and change constructor to `Animal(String name, int age)` (and update subclasses accordingly), or (b) remove `age` from the UML/problem statement and specify `Animal(String)` only.

issues.description: Seal/Pig/Goat constructors in the solution take only `(String name)`, but the UML/problem statement implies animals must initialize all Animal attributes and that `Animal` is constructed with `(String, int)` (name, age). If age is required, these subclass constructors should also accept `age` and call `super(name, age)`; otherwise the UML/spec should not include `age`.
issues.suggestedFix: If `age` is intended, change subclass constructors to `Seal(String name, int age)`, `Pig(String name, int age)`, `Goat(String name, int age)` and call `super(name, age)`. Otherwise, update UML/problem statement to remove `age` and state that constructors take only `name`.
